32610-the-long-arm.title: The Long Arm
32610-the-long-arm.creator: Unknown
32610-the-long-arm.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. While I sat thus, staring out with unseeing eyes at the rain which was by this time beating down smartly on the pavement, I became conscious that someone in the room was staring at me. I had not noticed that there was anyone else in the dark, low-ceilinged place except the obsequious proprietor who had served me my cigar and coffee. Now I realized that a man who sat in the corner diagonally across from me was studying me curiously from over his newspaper.

arxiv-2008-05139.title: Neumann-Rosochatius system for (m,n) string in A ​ d ​ S 3 × S 3 AdS_{3}\times S^{3} with mixed flux
arxiv-2008-05139.creator: Adrita Chakraborty, and Kamal L. Panigrahi
arxiv-2008-05139.description: Abstract S ​ L ​ ( 2 , ℤ ) SL(2,\mathbb{Z}) invariant action for probe ( m , n ) (m,n) string in A ​ d ​ S 3 × S 3 × T 4 AdS_{3}\times S^{3}\times T^{4} with mixed three-form fluxes can be described by an integrable deformation of an one-dimensional Neumann-Rosochatius (NR) system.

arxiv-2203-03550.title: When BERT Meets Quantum Temporal Convolution Learning for Text Classification in Heterogeneous Computing
arxiv-2203-03550.creator: Chao-Han Huck Yang 1 Jun Qi 1 Samuel Yen-Chi Chen 2 Yu Tsao 3 Pin-Yu Chen 4
arxiv-2203-03550.description: Abstract The rapid development of quantum computing has demonstrated many unique characteristics of quantum advantages, such as richer feature representation and more secured protection on model parameters. This work proposes a vertical federated learning architecture based on variational quantum circuits to demonstrate the competitive performance of a quantum-enhanced pre-trained BERT model for text classification.

arxiv-2306-05758.title: Interplay of Andreev reflection and Coulomb blockade in hybrid superconducting single electron transistors
arxiv-2306-05758.creator: Laura Sobral Rey, David Christian Ohnmacht, Clemens B. Winkelmann, Jens Siewert, Wolfgang Belzig, Elke Scheer
arxiv-2306-05758.description: Abstract We study the interplay between Coulomb blockade and superconductivity in a tunable superconductor-superconductor-normal metal single-electron transistor. The device is realized by connecting the superconducting island via an oxide barrier to the normal metal lead and with a break junction to the superconducting lead. The latter enables Cooper pair transport and (multiple) Andreev reflection.

arxiv-2402-14908.title: More Excitement Across the Horizon
arxiv-2402-14908.creator: María R. Preciado-Rivas, Manar Naeem, Robert B. Mann, Jorma Louko
arxiv-2402-14908.description: Abstract An Unruh-DeWitt detector falling radially into a four-dimensional Schwarzschild black hole, coupled linearly to a massless scalar field that has been prepared in the Hartle-Hawking or Unruh state, has recently been shown to exhibit a local extremum in its transition probability near the black hole horizon [K.K. Ng et al., New J. Phys. 24 (2022) 103018].

arxiv-2408-07696.title: Model-Based Control of Water Treatment with Pumped Water Storage
arxiv-2408-07696.creator: Ryan Mauery, Margaret Busse, Ilya Kovalenko
arxiv-2408-07696.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ryan Mauery, Margaret Busse, Ilya Kovalenko. Water treatment facilities are critical infrastructure they must accommodate dynamic demand patterns without system disruption. These patterns can be scheduled, such as daily residential irrigation, or unexpected, such as demand spikes from withdrawals for fire management. The critical necessity of clean, safe, and reliable water requires water treatment control strategies that are insensitive to disturbances to guarantee that demand will be met.

arxiv-2501-04330.title: Neural Parameter Estimation with Incomplete Data
arxiv-2501-04330.creator: Matthew Sainsbury-Dale, Andrew Zammit-Mangion, Noel Cressie, Raphaël Huser
arxiv-2501-04330.description: Abstract Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning have led to neural networks being used to generate lightning-speed answers to complex science questions, paintings in the style of Monet, or stories like those of Twain. Leveraging their computational speed and flexibility, neural networks are also being used to facilitate fast, likelihood-free statistical inference.

arxiv-2507-07193.title: Braneworld Dark Energy in light of DESI DR2
arxiv-2507-07193.creator: and Yuri Shtanov
arxiv-2507-07193.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by and Yuri Shtanov. Recent observational results from the DESI collaboration reveal tensions with the standard Λ \Lambda CDM model and favour a scenario in which dark energy (DE) decays over time. The DESI DR2 data also suggest that the DE equation of state (EoS) may have been phantom-like ( w < − 1 w<-1 ) in the past, evolving to w > − 1 w>-1 at present — implying a recent crossing of the phantom divide at w = − 1 w=-1 .

arxiv-2507-14535.title: Inference for Diffusion Processes via Controlled Sequential Monte Carlo and Splitting Schemes
arxiv-2507-14535.creator: S. Huang, R. G. Everitt, M. Tamborrino, A. M. Johansen
arxiv-2507-14535.description: Abstract We introduce an inferential framework for a wide class of semi-linear stochastic differential equations (SDEs). Recent work has shown that numerical splitting schemes can preserve critical properties of such types of SDEs, give rise to explicit pseudolikelihoods, and hence allow for parameter inference for fully observed processes.

arxiv-2512-21458.title: Non-loose torus knots in S 1 × S 2 S^{1}\times S^{2}
arxiv-2512-21458.creator: Jiaxin Huang, Youlin Li, Zaiting Xu
arxiv-2512-21458.description: Abstract . In this paper, we present a complete coarse classification of non-loose Legendrian and transverse torus knots in any contact structure on S 1 × S 2 S^{1}\times S^{2} . 1. Introduction A Legendrian or transverse knot in an overtwisted contact 3-manifold is called non-loose if its complement is tight.

pmc-12553115.title: A Toaster in the Bathroom: Neural Correlates of Semantic Construction During Episodic Memory Recall
pmc-12553115.creator: Carina Zoellner, Rebekka Heinen, Nicole Klein, Nora A. Herweg, Christian J. Merz, Oliver T. Wolf
pmc-12553115.description: When recalling what you ate for breakfast last Wednesday, you might not remember the exact meal, but you may confidently select the items you typically eat. Here, semantic knowledge (i.e., what you usually eat) contributes to the reconstructive process of episodic memory retrieval (i.e., what you actually ate).

pmc-12596978.title: Conservative and surgical management of small bowel diverticulitis complicated by enteroliths: A case report
pmc-12596978.creator: Richard Lee, Jill Jozefowicz, Theodore Niemann
pmc-12596978.description: IntroductionSmall bowel diverticulitis with enterolith-associated small bowel obstruction is a rare complication which can lead to significant morbidity and mortality. Here we present a case of small bowel diverticulitis which underwent successful conservative management at the time of initial presentation but required a surgical intervention for enterolith-associated small bowel obstruction during a subsequent hospitalization.

pmc-12804783.title: Predicting and classifying type 2 diabetes using a transparent ensemble model combining random forest, k-nearest neighbor, and neural networks
pmc-12804783.creator: Niloufar Zaferani, Mohammad Reza Afrash, Khadijeh Moulaei
pmc-12804783.description: Diabetes is one of the major health challenges in today’s world, since chronic elevation of blood sugar can cause serious and sometimes irreparable damage to organs such as the heart, kidneys, and nervous system. Early detection of this disease plays a vital role in reducing its complications.

pmc-13038723.title: Accuracy of dynamic computer-assisted implant surgery among novice operators using three different patient registration methods: an in-vitro study
pmc-13038723.creator: Ryo Yamamoto, Toshiki Nojiri, Daichi Yoshida, Yutaro Oyamada, Akihiro Fukutoku, Kazuhiro Kon
pmc-13038723.description: IntroductionAccurate implant placement with computer-assisted implant surgery (CAIS) is critical to ensuring long-term success. Dynamic computer-assisted implant surgery (d-CAIS) enhances surgical precision through real-time feedback; however, its accuracy and procedural efficiency when used by novice operators remain insufficiently investigated. This study evaluated how different registration methods in d-CAIS influence implant placement accuracy and procedural time when performed by novice operators.

pmc-13184998.title: Medial‐pivot total knee arthroplasty demonstrates more constrained mid‐flexion gait kinematics than posterior‐stabilised total knee arthroplasty under standardised soft‐tissue balancing: A randomised controlled trial with a healthy reference cohort
pmc-13184998.creator: Eiichi Nakamura, Nobukazu Okamoto, Tetsuro Masuda, Satoshi Hisanaga, Masaki Yugami, Yasunari Oniki, Takeshi Miyamoto
pmc-13184998.description: PurposeMost contemporary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) designs aim to replicate native kinematics, yet the independent contribution of implant geometry to dynamic stability remains unclear when soft‐tissue balance is standardised. We compared medial‐pivot (MP) and posterior‐stabilised (PS) TKA implanted under a uniform medial‐tight balancing protocol and contrasted both with healthy knees.

pmc-13197648.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesTo explore the latent profiles of symptom severity among systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients and analyze the influencing factors associated with these different latent profiles, providing clinical evidence for the management of SLE symptoms.MethodsUsing convenience sampling, a questionnaire survey was conducted among SLE patients at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University employing the SLE Symptom Checklist (SSC) between November 2022 and July 2023.

pmc-13341120.title: PertAdapt: unlocking single-cell foundation models for genetic perturbation prediction via condition-sensitive adaptation
pmc-13341120.creator: Ding Bai, Le Song, Eric P Xing
pmc-13341120.description: MotivationSingle-cell foundation models (FMs) pretrained on massive unlabeled scRNA-seq data show strong potential in predicting transcriptional responses to unseen genetic perturbations (e.g. knockouts, variants). However, existing approaches do not effectively transfer pretrained knowledge and overlook the imbalance between perturbation-sensitive and insensitive genes, yielding only marginal improvements over non-pretrained baselines.

pmc-13579257.creator: Nishanth Thalambedu, Krishna Vasipalli, Nikhila Sampath Kumar, Sruthi Vellanki, Anup Kumar Trikannad, Manoja Gullapalli, Shi Ming Tu, Anuradha Kunthur
pmc-13579257.description: Immunotherapy has changed the landscape of bladder cancer treatment in recent years, both for localized and metastatic bladder cancer. While bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) remains the gold standard for high-risk non–muscle-invasive bladder cancer, the development of checkpoint inhibitors continues to increase treatment options for patients who are intolerant or unresponsive to BCG.
